LESSON: NUTRITION IN PLANTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 2.1: Nutrition in plants
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Nutrition in plants, part of Living Things and their Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 INTEGRATED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How do plants obtain nutrients? 2. Why is photosynthesis important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Nutrition in plants together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: The learner studies independently while using charts or photomicrographs or non-print media to observe

and discuss the internal structure of the leaf in relation to their roles in photosynthesis.

11

● Self-efficacy: The learner develops leadership skills while working in groups to discuss the process and products of

photosynthesis.

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner observes safety precautions while carrying out experiments to show that light, carbon (IV) oxide

and chlorophyll are necessary for photosynthesis.

● Social justice: The learner shares resources equitably while carrying out experiments to show that light, carbon (IV) oxide

and chlorophyll are necessary for photosynthesis.

● Integrity: The learner displays honesty while carrying out experiments to show that light, carbon (IV) oxide and chlorophyll

are necessary for photosynthesis and presenting their own results.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental education and climate change: The learner collects only the required number of specimens of plants to

observe and discuss the external structure of the leaf in relation to their roles in photosynthesis.

Link to other subjects:

● Agriculture and Nutrition: The information on photosynthesis is linked to food production.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Print and tactile charts of the internal parts of a leaf, light microscope, digital devices with assistive technology such as adapted

keyboard, screen readers and screen magnifiers, print materials in appropriate font and colour contrast and braille materials and

equipment.
